study_identification_part.si_4_title: Revealing Individual Neuroanatomical Heterogeneity in Alzheimer Disease Using Neuroanatomical Normative Modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Reference dataset combined multiple public sources (OASIS, ABCD, UKB). Clinical target data came from ADNI. OASIS version not specified; recorded as OASIS-1 to match allowed categories.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The reference data set was made by combining data on healthy people from multiple publicly available sources, 27 including OASIS, Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, and UKB, detailed in eTable 1 (links.lww.com/WNL/ C774). The clinical data used in the preparation of this article were obtained from the ADNI database.

answer.OASIS-1: reference dataset for normative model training (healthy participants)

answer.ABCD: reference dataset for normative model training (healthy participants)

answer.UK Biobank: reference dataset for normative model training (healthy participants)

answer.ADNI: clinical target dataset; ADNI controls used for model recalibration and remaining controls/MCI/AD used for heterogeneity assessment

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Reference dataset sources (OASIS/ABCD/UKB) are used to build the normative model; ADNI provides the clinical target data and calibration controls for transfer to ADNI sites.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: The reference data set was made by combining data on healthy people from multiple publicly available sources, 27 including OASIS, Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, and UKB, detailed in eTable 1 (links.lww.com/WNL/ C774). The clinical data used in the preparation of this article were obtained from the ADNI database. The parameters of the reference normative model were recalibrated to the ADNI data set using 70% of healthy controls per ADNI site... The remaining 30% of healthy controls plus MCI and patients with AD were used to assess the heterogeneity in neuroanatomical presentation.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Reference dataset of healthy participants used to train the normative model; ADNI controls used for recalibration (70% per site) but count not reported.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: A neuroanatomical normative model indexed cortical thickness distributions using a separate healthy reference data set (n = 33,072), which used hierarchical Bayesian regression to predict cortical thickness per region using age and sex, while adjusting for site noise.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age summary statistics for the reference dataset used in normative model training are not reported; only described as spanning the human lifespan.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: Participants were derived from 2 data sets: (1) a reference data set that comprised healthy people across the human lifespan

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex breakdown for the reference dataset used to train the normative model is not reported.
